thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @maya - High error rate observed for tenant 'acme-corp' on dedicated pool dp-54. 500s spike for function-calling endpoints starting 1755551220. Alert: fc_error_rate > 8% for 5m.
maya: I’m on it. Looking at logs for dp-54 now.
maya: quick grep shows a LOT of ParserError in the function-calling path. Example: 
```
ERROR ParserError: Unexpected field 'user_metadata' at position 2
    at parseArgs (/srv/runtime/parser.js:214:15)
    at FunctionCallHandler (/srv/runtime/handler.js:78:9)
```
maya: The errors line up with a customer deploy at ~1755551200 per request traces. Suspect schema drift from their new tool-caller payload.
liam: tagging in. Is this isolated to acme-corp or affecting other tenants?
maya: so far only acme-corp tenant id t-acme-11. No cross-tenant errors on same pool from other tenants. Looks like the parser is blowing up when optional fields appear.
priya: if it's tenant-specific, we should isolate the tenant to avoid noisy neighbors. Options: move to a fresh dedicated slot or route to backup pool. Any preference?
maya: recommend routing to dp-77 (warm standby) with older parser binary that tolerates extra keys. Can do a per-tenant route override.
sam: create a quick routing rule? I can push a config change to route t-acme-11 -> dp-77 for reads. Will that also affect writes?
maya: it needs to cover function-calling (fc) and chat-to-fc gateway. Make it for all fc endpoints for that tenant. Also enable strict schema fallback on dp-77 so it ignores unknown keys.
caroline: I'm on standby to notify the customer. Do we have an ETA for a mitigation? They are in the middle of a major rollout.
maya: mitigation (routing) in ~5m. Then follow with rollback/patch. Will update.
deploy-bot: rollouts: Starting config change deploy by sam (sam) — routing-rule add: tenant=t-acme-11 -> pool=dp-77 (canary 100%)
sam: pushed route change. Verifying connectivity.
maya: verifying error rate post-route. 
maya: error rate dropped from 9.6% -> 0.4% in the fc path for that tenant. Logs now show requests served by dp-77 with older parser. :white_check_mark:
priya: nice. Root cause plan? Seems the customer's tool started sending an additional `user_metadata` object which our newer parser treats as reserved. That’s schema drift.
liam: can we make runtime parser tolerant by default? Is there a quick toggle?
maya: there's a feature flag to enable lenient field acceptance but it requires binary that isn't rolled to dp-54 yet. Short-term: keep tenant on dp-77. Medium-term: ship lenient parser to dp-54 and run canary.
priya: also open a bridge with customer engineering to confirm payload change. Caroline, can you ask them to roll back or confirm schema?
caroline: on it. Messaging them now: "We're seeing parser failures due to new field in payload; routing you to a safe pool while we investigate. Please confirm whether the field is intentional."
caroline: customer says the field was added intentionally as part of 3rd-party SDK update. They can rollback, but prefer we support it.
maya: ok. We'll plan to make parser tolerant. Steps: 1) keep tenant on dp-77 2) backport lenient parser to dp-54 in a canary (dp-54-canary) 3) run smoke with acme corp dev traffic 4) if green, move tenant back and then ship global patch.
liam: who owns the backport? I can pick it up.
maya: assign to liam for backport + canary rollout. sam will coordinate routing changes. Priya to own incident coordination and postmortem. Caroline will own customer comms.
liam: starting work now. ETA for canary build ~45m.
deploy-bot: build pipeline: started build for runtime/parser-lenient (sha ab12f3) triggered by liam.
maya: also added a temporary alert to detect fc parser errors per-tenant (threshold 1%).
priya: reminder to log an incident ticket and link customer case. I'll create INC-2026-322.
priya: handoff: maya is going to bed in ~30m, tagging liam as primary oncall after canary done.
maya: handing off to @liam in 35m. I’ll leave monitoring and runbook notes in the ticket.
liam: acknowledged. I’ll follow through on canary and coordinate promotion.
caroline: customer acknowledged and appreciates quick routing fix. They requested a short postmortem and a timeline for permanent support.
liam: canary built and deployed to dp-54-canary. Running 10% of acme test traffic. Logs look clean so far.
liam: smoke pass OK. No ParserError for 30m on canary.
liam: promoting tenant back to dp-54 main. Doing 50% -> 100% in 5m.
deploy-bot: rollout: promotion to dp-54 main by liam initiated.
maya: (after handoff) thanks team, leaving notes in INC-2026-322. :wave:
liam: promotion done. Monitoring. Error rate stable at baseline.
priya: incident resolved for customer impact. Follow-ups: postmortem, automatic schema leniency flag on by default for fc workloads, and long-term: add a cached schema registry for tenant-specific schemas.
caroline: I've scheduled a customer debrief for tomorrow 10am PT. I'll attach logs and steps taken.
priya: closing out on-call pages. Will assign postmortem owners and link to ticket.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-322 transitioned to resolved state by priya.
maya: good work. Please add a note about making parser tests include unexpected fields as part of CI.
liam: will do.
caroline: customer happy with routing and timeline. They asked for SLA note. I’ll draft.
priya: thanks everyone.
